assessment.claims_boundary: Funding, manufacturing programs, and vendor roadmaps are leading indicators only. They do not demonstrate Q-day, a production cryptanalytic attack machine, or a production key break.

evidence.name: CHIPS R&D quantum program
evidence.statement: Commerce announced letters of intent with nine companies totaling $2 billion in planned CHIPS R&D support for quantum computing, including fault-tolerant and manufacturing bottlenecks.

evidence.name: Quantinuum finalized CHIPS award
evidence.statement: Commerce finalized an award of up to $100 million addressing manufacturing bottlenecks for scalable fault-tolerant trapped-ion quantum computers.

evidence.name: Rigetti finalized CHIPS award
evidence.statement: Commerce finalized an award of up to $100 million for superconducting quantum-computing scaling, including readout electronics, cryostats, and fabrication capability.

evidence.name: D-Wave finalized CHIPS award
evidence.statement: Commerce finalized an award of up to $100 million for annealing and gate-model superconducting quantum-computing process technologies, packaging, coherence, and error-rate improvements.

evidence.name: GlobalFoundries quantum manufacturing award
evidence.statement: GlobalFoundries and Commerce finalized a $375 million R&D award intended to scale domestic quantum semiconductor manufacturing and move quantum hardware from research/prototyping toward commercial-scale production.

evidence.name: Treasury Quantum-Readiness Task Force
evidence.statement: Treasury launched a public-private financial-sector PQ transition task force with digital assets and emerging-technology risk explicitly in scope.

prohibited_inferences: These awards do not prove that any funded company will meet its roadmap.
Manufacturing scale does not equal cryptanalytic capability.
Financial-sector migration does not equal blockchain-level PQ activation.
No production cryptocurrency key break is established by this record.
